source.original_text:
For a compact-state process on [0,T], the sums of second-order Taylor residuals over the dyadic grids converge in measure to zero whenever the sums of squared increments converge in measure to a real-valued Q.

The sample space Ω carries a finite measure μ. E is a locally compact real normed space with its Borel measurable structure. K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. Each time evaluation of the K-valued process X is measurable. Its paths are continuous on the specified compact time domain for μ-almost every sample.
T>0, X is defined at all nonnegative times and has almost-sure continuous paths on [0,T]. The dyadic sums of squared increments converge in measure to Q:Ω→ℝ.

\sum_{i<2^n}R_f(X_{iT/2^n},X_{(i+1)T/2^n}-X_{iT/2^n})\xrightarrow{\mu}0.

blind_reconstruction.text:
Finite measure space (Omega,m,mu); locally compact real normed space E with its Borel measurable structure; compact K⊆E; f:E→R; K-valued stochastic path X; real random variable Q.

E is a normed additive commutative group and real normed vector space, locally compact, with measurable and Borel-space instances. T>0 is a nonnegative real. X:[0,infinity)×Omega→K (subtype), Q:Omega→R.

Assumptions: mu finite; K compact; f is C² at each point of K in E. For every t≥0, X(t,·) is measurable into K. For mu-a.e. omega, t↦X(t,omega) is continuous on [0,T]. With t_i^n=iT/2^n and Delta_i^n X=X(t_{i+1}^n)-X(t_i^n) interpreted in E, ∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}||Delta_i^n X||² converges in mu-measure to Q as n→infinity. No separate measurability or integrability hypothesis on Q is written.

Conclusion: Define R_f(x,v)=f(x+v)-f(x)-Df(x)[v]-(1/2)D²f(x)[v,v]. Then omega↦∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}R_f(X(t_i^n,omega),Delta_i^n X(omega)) converges in mu-measure to the identically zero function.

Quantifier order: For arbitrary listed data satisfying the assumptions, convergence in measure of the dyadic squared-increment sums to the supplied Q implies convergence in measure of the dyadic second-order Taylor-remainder sums to zero.

Scope: One fixed positive horizon; dyadic mesh; convergence in measure only, not an asserted L¹ or almost-sure convergence. Derivatives are ambient Frechet derivatives; x+v need not independently be constrained by a neighborhood assumption.

Constant dependencies: Q is supplied, arbitrary subject to the stated convergence; no rate or uniform constant is asserted.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoTaylorGridRemainder
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.FiniteTimeGrid
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.DyadicElementaryRefinement

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoDyadicTaylorRemainder

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.CompactTaylorRemainder
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoTaylorGridRemainder
open FiniteTimeGrid ElementaryItoIntegral SampledElementaryApproximation DyadicElementaryRefinement

/-- The Taylor remainder limit on the regular dyadic grids used for
completed Itô integrals and quadratic variation. -/
theorem tendstoInMeasure_dyadic_sum_secondOrderRemainder
    {Ω E : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [LocallyCompactSpace E]
    [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] {K : Set E}
    (hK : IsCompact K) (f : E → ℝ) (hf : ∀ x ∈ K, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    {T : ℝ≥0} (hT : 0 < T) (X : ℝ≥0 → Ω → K) (hX : ∀ t, Measurable (X t))
    (hpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => X t ω) (Icc 0 T))
    {Q : Ω → ℝ}
    (hQV : TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω =>
      let times := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
      ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), ‖(X (times i.succ) ω : E) - (X (times i.castSucc) ω : E)‖ ^ 2)
      atTop Q) :
    TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω =>
      let times := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
      ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), secondOrderRemainder f (X (times i.castSucc) ω : E)
        ((X (times i.succ) ω : E) - (X (times i.castSucc) ω : E))) atTop (fun _ => 0) := by
  let times (n : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T n) (2 ^ n)
  let S := Icc (0 : ℝ≥0) T
  have : CompactSpace S := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp isCompact_Icc
  have htime (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) : times n i ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT n) _).monotone (Fin.le_last i)).trans_eq
      (regularDyadic_last_time T n)
  let grid (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (2 ^ n + 1)) : S := ⟨times n i, bot_le, htime n i⟩
  let Y (t : S) := X (t : ℝ≥0)
  have hY (t : S) : Measurable (Y t) := hX t
  have hYpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Continuous (fun t : S => Y t ω) :=
    hpaths.mono fun _ hω => hω.domRestrict
  have hmesh (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ i : Fin (2 ^ n),
      dist (grid n i.succ) (grid n i.castSucc) < δ := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_dyadicMesh_lt T hδ] with n hn i
    change dist ((times n i.succ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) ((times n i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) < δ
    have h := dyadic_activeCell_right (T := T) i
    change times n i.succ = times n i.castSucc + dyadicMesh T n at h
    rw [h, NNReal.coe_add, Real.dist_eq, add_sub_cancel_left, abs_of_nonneg (NNReal.coe_nonneg _)]
    exact hn
  exact tendstoInMeasure_sum_secondOrderRemainder_of_quadraticVariation hK f hf Y hY
    hYpaths (fun n => 2 ^ n) grid hmesh hQV

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoDyadicTaylorRemainder

steps.title: Restrict time to the compact interval
steps.text: Every dyadic time lies in [0,T]. Restrict X to this interval, retaining measurable time slices and almost-sure path continuity.
steps.lean:

steps.text: Consecutive grid points are exactly T/2ⁿ apart, so their distances tend to zero. All hypotheses of the arbitrary-grid residual theorem now hold.

    exact hn
